Sure, here is the summary for the Summary of Attack Methods section of the paper:

The paper proposes a novel jailbreak method targeting Large Language Models (LLMs) called Adaptive Position Pre-Filled Jailbreak Attack (AdaPPA). The method exploits the model's instruction-following capabilities and narrative-shifting abilities to generate harmful content. The approach consists of three steps: (1) low-rank training on pre-filling content generation and question rewriting models, (2) inputting questions into both models to obtain rewritten questions and pre-filled content, and (3) combining the content in various ways to attack the target model. The method improves the attack success rate by 47% compared to existing approaches on 10 classic black-box models. The key innovation is the use of pre-filled content to trick the model into generating harmful content, which has not been explored in previous research.

Sure, here is the summary for the Introduction to the Mechanism of Success:

The paper "Adaptive Position Pre-Fill Jailbreak Attack Approach Targeting LLMs" proposes a novel approach to jailbreak attacks on large language models (LLMs) that leverages the model's instruction-following capabilities and narrative-shifting abilities to generate harmful content. The authors observe that existing attack methods primarily focus on the semantic level and overlook the difference in the model's alignment protection capabilities at different output stages. They propose an adaptive position pre-fill jailbreak attack approach that exploits the model's ability to follow instructions by pre-filling output positions with adaptively generated content of various types, including both safe and harmful content. The approach significantly improves the attack success rate compared to existing approaches on 10 classic black-box models. The authors contribute to the observation of the effectiveness and difference of generating harmful content by pre-filling the output of LLMs with text of different lengths and types, and the proposal of a novel jailbreak method targeting LLMs that utilizes the shallow alignment vulnerability of the model and employs a combination of safe and harmful responses to enhance successful jailbreak attacks.

The related work section of this paper primarily focuses on jailbreak attacks targeting Large Language Models (LLMs). The authors discuss existing research on jailbreak attacks, including gradient optimization [4], [5], jailbreak prompt search [6], [7], and red team search [8], [9].
